title: Maximum Product Subarray
description:
# Maximum Product Subarray

Given an integer array `nums`, return the largest product of any non-empty contiguous subarray.

A contiguous subarray is one nonempty segment of the original array, retaining every element within it. It may contain `0`, but you cannot delete an interior zero and join the two sides.

The answer is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

## Example 1

**Input:** `nums = [2,3,-2,4]`

**Output:** `6`

**Explanation:** The subarray `[2,3]` has product `6`.

## Example 2

**Input:** `nums = [-2,0,-1]`

**Output:** `0`

**Explanation:** `[-2,-1]` is not contiguous because `0` is between them, so the best product is `0`.

## Constraints

- `1 <= nums.length <= 2 * 10^4`
- `-10 <= nums[i] <= 10`
- The product of any prefix or suffix of `nums` is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit signed integer.

solutions.name: Rolling Max-Min Product State
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan the array while maintaining the maximum and minimum product of a subarray that must end at the current index. When the current value is negative, swap those two ending products before extending them.

## Key Insight

The minimum ending product is not useless. A very negative product can become the next maximum after multiplication by another negative value. The current value itself is also a possible fresh subarray start.

## Complexity Analysis

The scan touches each element once, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. Only three running values are stored, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: DP Arrays for Ending Products
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build two arrays: `maxEnding[i]` is the largest product of a subarray ending at `i`, and `minEnding[i]` is the smallest product ending at `i`. Each cell considers the current value alone, extending the previous maximum, and extending the previous minimum.

## Key Insight

Writing the full table makes the state definition explicit before compressing it to constant space. The three candidates are necessary because the sign of `nums[i]` decides whether the previous maximum or previous minimum is useful.

## Complexity Analysis

Each index is processed once with constant work, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. The two teaching arrays use `O(n)` space.

solutions.name: Prefix and Suffix Zero-Reset Scan
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from the left and from the right at the same time, resetting a running product after it becomes zero. For every position, update the answer with both the prefix-side product and the suffix-side product.

## Key Insight

Within a zero-free segment, if there is an odd number of negatives, the best product drops either the prefix through the first negative or the suffix from the last negative. A left-to-right and right-to-left scan observes both possibilities.

## Complexity Analysis

The array is scanned once from both directions, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. The scan stores only two running products and the answer, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: Zero-Split Negative Boundary Analysis
solutions.description:
## Approach

Zeros split the array into independent nonzero segments. For each segment, multiply the whole segment and count negative values. If the count is even, the full segment is best for that segment. If the count is odd, drop either the prefix through the first negative or the suffix from the last negative.

## Key Insight

This route derives the answer from segment structure rather than ending-state DP. It explains why zeros reset the problem and why only the first and last negative boundaries matter inside a nonzero segment.

## Complexity Analysis

Every element is visited a constant number of times across segment scans, so the time complexity is `O(n)`. Only segment counters and products are stored, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.

solutions.name: Brute Force Rolling Product Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Enumerate every possible start index. For each start, extend the end index one step at a time while maintaining the rolling product of that exact contiguous subarray.

## Key Insight

The baseline is slower, but it is the clearest correctness reference: every non-empty contiguous subarray is considered exactly once, and no non-contiguous combination can enter the answer.

## Complexity Analysis

There are `O(n^2)` start-end ranges and each extension updates the product in constant time, so the time complexity is `O(n^2)`. Only the rolling product and best answer are stored, so the space complexity is `O(1)`.
